newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Syria says Israel on path of confrontation.
newsitem.headline: Syria says Israel on path of confrontation.

text.p: Syria, sniping from the sidelines at the Middle East crisis summit in Washington, said on Wednesday Israel had chosen confrontation and warned the Jewish state it would pay a heavy price.

Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara told the U.N. General Assembly in a speech that the recent Israeli-Palestinian clashes in the West Bank and Gaza showed that the new right-wing Israeli government had turned away from peace.
"One may conclude that this Israeli government has no strategy for peace and that it has chosen, as it appears, the path of confrontation," Shara said.
"The path of confrontation is however very costly...because Israel can start a war whenever it chooses, but it cannot end it as it chooses," he said.

Syria, a key player in the Middle East peace process, is not involved in the Washington summit which has brought together Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

Last week, Shara said the violent clashes between Israelis and Palestinians showed the whole peace process was dying. He did not repeat that on Wednesday, but accused the Israeli government of trying "to demolish all the achievements of the past five years".
He quoted Syrian President Hafez al-Assad as saying he did not believe there was "any window for a just and comprehensive peace" if Israel stuck to its current policies.
Syria wants the return of the Golan, seized by Israel in 1967, as the main condition for making peace with the Jewish state.
